data.description:
# Spend the full monthly OpenCode Go allowance before it resets (quota-aware surge)

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want the proxy to steer more traffic to `opencode-*`
provider entries in proportion to the monthly allowance each account still has
and how close its reset is, **and to remove the `available_times` restrictions on
any `opencode-*` entry that still has allowance during the final week before its
reset**, so that each monthly Go/Go Plus allowance is fully spent (ideally
finishing on the last day) instead of expiring unused.

## Problem / background

OpenCode Go allowances are **use-it-or-lose-it**: usage limits are defined as
monthly dollar amounts per model, with a rolling-5-hour window at 20% of the
monthly cap and a weekly window at 50% (`https://opencode.ai/docs/go`). Any
allowance still unspent at `resetsAt` is simply lost — no carry-over.

Today the proxy is blind to how much of that allowance is left:

- `available_times` (LP-0MS4ETBNO0022QAC) gates every `opencode-go*` DeepSeek
  entry to the **off-peak** UTC windows (`00:00-01:00`, `04:00-06:00`,
  `10:00-00:00`) purely for pricing reasons, regardless of whether the account
  is sitting at 5% or 95% of its monthly cap.
- Routing order inside the `opencode-go*` chain is static; three accounts
  (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_2_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_3_API_KEY`) are tried in
  config order with no awareness of which one has allowance left.
- The proxy only learns about exhaustion **reactively**, from a
  `GoUsageLimitError` / 429 body (`proxy/provider.py:4363`,
  LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ, LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8). The bug fixed in
  LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8 was triggered by guessing reset times; a proactive,
  authoritative reading removes the guesswork entirely.

Consequence today: a key can finish a monthly period at 88% (observed, below)
while another sits at 5%, and the residual allowance on every key expires
unspent at the end of each period.

## Discovery findings (verified live 2026-10-19 ~10:22–10:25 UTC)

Facts established by probing the gateway directly with the existing keys; the
implementation should not need to re-derive these.

1. **Response headers carry no quota information.** `POST
   https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` returns only `date`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, `cf-placement`, `x-opencode-log-id`,
   `x-zen-model`, `server`, `cf-ray`. No `x-ratelimit-*`, no `retry-after`, no
   reset hints, on success **or** on error. Response body `usage` carries token
   counts only — no cost/price/remaining figures.
2. **The authoritative quota source is `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage`**
   (Bearer key, no `x-opencode-session` needed, `cache-control: no-store`):

   ```json
   {"usage":{"rolling":{"status":"ok","percent":0,"resetsAt":"2026-10-19T15:22:54.000Z"},
             "weekly":{"status":"ok","percent":0,"resetsAt":"2026-10-26T00:00:00.000Z"},
             "monthly":{"status":"ok","percent":88,"resetsAt":"2026-10-23T08:43:55.000Z"}}}
   ```
3. **Quota is per API key (per account), not per model, and the endpoint takes no
   model selector** — `?model=…` and `?detailed=true` are silently ignored and
   return the same aggregate. The per-model dollar limits documented on the Go
   page are therefore not observable through this API.
4. **Live readings at time of writing** (shows the problem concretely — two of
   three accounts are close to exhaustion, one is nearly untouched):

   | entry | `api_key_env` | rolling | weekly | monthly | monthly `resetsAt` |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | `opencode-go` | `OPENCODE_API_KEY` | 0% | 0% | **88%** | 2026-10-23T08:43:55Z |
   | `opencode-go-2` | `OPENCODE_2_API_KEY` | 0% | 0% | **95%** | 2026-10-30T00:03:43Z |
   | `opencode-go-3` | `OPENCODE_3_API_KEY` | 3% | 1% | 5% | 2026-11-17T10:05:09Z |
5. **Reset dates are per account and are not calendar-aligned** (the three keys
   reset 7 days apart), so the surge window must be computed per account from its
   own `resetsAt`, not from a fixed calendar rule.
6. `rolling.resetsAt` behaves like "end of the current 5-hour window"
   (≈ now + 5 h) rather than "unblock time"; the `weekly.resetsAt` is
   week-aligned.
7. **Peak vs off-peak pricing matters for quota burn rate**: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
   is $0.15/$0.60 per 1M tokens off-peak and $0.30/$1.20 peak (peak hours
   `01:00-04:00` and `06:00-10:00` UTC, Mon–Fri). Because the monthly allowance
   is a *dollar* amount, tokens spent in peak hours deplete it twice as fast.
8. Model IDs: `opencode-go` serves only `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and
   `deepseek-v4-pro`; `deepseek-v4-flash` exists only on the plain `deepseek`
   provider. Requests need an `x-opencode-session` header (the proxy already
   synthesises it, `tests/test_opencode_session_header.py`).
9. There are **no** `/v1/credits`, `/v1/billing`, `/v1/quota`, `/v1/me` or
   `/v1/account` endpoints (all 404). The console-only "Use balance"
   pay-as-you-go fallback is not API-visible — see the cost guard below.

## Requirements

- **R1 — Quota poller.** Poll `GET /v1/usage` per distinct `api_key_env` on a
  configurable interval, cache the result, de-duplicate concurrent polls per
  account, and fail open (keep the last known values, log at WARN) on error,
  timeout or malformed JSON.
- **R2 — Derived state.** From each poll derive, per account: `monthly_headroom =
  100 - monthly.percent`, `weekly_headroom`, `rolling_headroom`,
  `seconds_to_reset`, and an `exhausted` flag. The **effective headroom is the
  minimum of the three windows** — the monthly cap is irrelevant if the 5-hour
  or weekly window is already spent.
- **R3 — Headroom-aware ordering.** Within the `opencode-go*` chain, order
  eligible entries by descending quota urgency score
  (`effective_headroom / seconds_to_reset`, producer decision Q2 → 2c),
  stable tie-break on the existing config order, so traffic goes to the
  account that can absorb it most before its own reset. An
  entry whose effective headroom is below the exhaustion threshold is treated as
  unavailable for routing (same effect as a cooldown, but derived from quota
  rather than from a 429).
- **R4 — Final-week surge (removes date restrictions).** When
  `0 < seconds_to_reset <= quota_surge_days` (default 7) **and** the entry is not
  exhausted, `available_times` gating is bypassed for that entry: it becomes
  eligible at any UTC hour, and this is logged once per state change with
  `reason=quota_surge`. The bypass clears automatically when the entry becomes
  exhausted or when its reset passes.
- **R5 — Pacing that front-loads spend without stranding quota.** Within the
  surge window the dispatch preference must increase with remaining headroom and
  with diminishing time-to-reset, targeting roughly 100% consumption at
  `resetsAt` — but the ramp must be *achievable*, i.e. it must respect the
  rolling (20%) and weekly (50%) caps, because a large residual cannot be
  discharged in a last-minute burst. Surge must therefore start ramping before
  the final week whenever the residual is large, so the last day finishes the
  quota rather than trying to finish it all at once.
- **R6 — Prefer cheaper tokens first.** Surge ordering prefers windows that are
  already `available_times`-eligible (off-peak) and only uses peak hours when the
  residual is projected to be unspendable otherwise. Peak hours burn allowance at
  2x the rate (finding 7).
- **R7 — Hard stop / cost guard.** Never dispatch to an entry whose monthly
  `percent` is at or above `quota_exhaustion_percent` (default 99.5), and never
  after a `GoUsageLimitError`. This must hold *especially* if the account has the
  console "Use balance" option enabled, where over-consumption would spend real
  pay-as-you-go money. Surge bypasses **only** `available_times` — never
  `rate_limit_rpm`, the sibling-failure circuit breaker, failure-domain grouping
  or stall/quarantine gates.
- **R8 — Observability.** Log every poll, every surge enter/exit, every ordering
  decision and every quota-driven skip, at a level that fits the existing log
  volume (polls/transitions at INFO, per-request ordering at DEBUG). Expose the
  derived per-account quota state in the existing metrics/status surfaces so an
  operator can answer "how much is left, when does it reset, is surge active".
- **R9 — Off by default is not required, but a kill switch is.** Configuration
  must allow the whole behaviour to be disabled (`server.quota_surge_enabled:
  false`) and a dry-run mode that emits the routing decisions it *would* make
  without changing routing.
- **R10 — Documentation.** `config.yaml` documents every new key with its
  default, and `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` explains the pacing model, the peak/
  off-peak trade-off and the reset-alignment caveat.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — With a stubbed `/v1/usage` transport, the poller issues at most one
  request per account per `server.quota_poll_interval_seconds` (default 900 s)
  no matter how many client requests arrive, and concurrent pollers coalesce
  into a single in-flight request per account. A poll failure (500, timeout,
  malformed body) leaves the previous values intact, logs at WARN, and never
  fails or delays a client request.
- **AC2** — Derived state is exposed (metrics/status surface) as, per account:
  `rolling/weekly/monthly percent`, `resetsAt`, `seconds_to_reset`,
  `effective_headroom`, `surge_active`, `exhausted`. Verified by a test that
  feeds a known `/v1/usage` payload and asserts the exposed values, including
  that `effective_headroom` is the **minimum** of the three windows (feed
  `rolling=95, weekly=10, monthly=40` and assert effective headroom is 5).
- **AC3** — Given `opencode-go` at monthly 88% and `opencode-go-3` at 5% with
  both eligible, the routing decision prefers `opencode-go-3`. Reversing the
  percentages reverses the preference. Equal headroom falls back to config order
  (deterministic).
- **AC4** — An entry whose monthly `percent >= 99.5` (or effective headroom
  below the threshold) is skipped without any upstream request being attempted,
  and the skip is logged with the reason. Repeated over a table of window
  combinations.
- **AC5** — Final-week bypass: with `resetsAt` 6 days away and monthly 50%, an
  entry configured with `available_times: ["10:00-00:00"]` is eligible at a
  simulated 02:00 UTC (previously ineligible) and the eligibility is logged with
  `reason=quota_surge`. With `resetsAt` 8 days away the same entry at 02:00 UTC
  remains ineligible (unchanged behaviour).
- **AC6** — The bypass is scoped to `available_times` only: with surge active, an
  entry that is rate-limited (`rate_limit_rpm`), circuit-broken, or in a
  usage-limit quarantine is still skipped. Verified by a test that activates
  surge and simultaneously trips each of those gates.
- **AC7** — Pacing function is unit-tested over a table of
  `(effective_headroom, seconds_to_reset)` pairs and satisfies: (a) monotonically
  non-decreasing in headroom at fixed time-to-reset; (b) monotonically
  non-decreasing as reset approaches at fixed headroom; (c) returns the baseline
  (no-surge) preference outside the surge window; (d) a large residual with a
  near reset yields a higher preference than a small residual with a distant
  reset for the same entry; (e) never yields a preference that would exceed the
  rolling/w weekly cap in a single 5-hour window (asserted against the documented
  20%/50% relationship).
- **AC8** — With `server.quota_surge_enabled: false`, routing decisions are
  byte-identical to today's behaviour for a table of representative requests
  (existing `available_times` and ordering tests continue to pass unchanged). In
  dry-run mode the computed decisions are logged but routing is unchanged.
- **AC9** — A stale-quota guard: when the last successful poll is older than
  `server.quota_state_max_age_seconds` (default 3600 s), surge is suspended and
  the proxy reverts to configured `available_times` (fail-safe, not fail-open),
  logged at WARN.
- **AC10** — Hard stop: a simulated `monthly.percent = 99.6` (or a
  `GoUsageLimitError` response) mid-surge stops surge for that account on the
  very next dispatch decision, with zero further requests to that entry in the
  same test, and the existing quarantine path from LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ still
  applies.
- **AC11** — Tests cover the poller, derivation, ordering, bypass, pacing, guards
  and kill switch (unit + at least one integration test against a fake upstream),
  all green, and the existing suite is unaffected.
- **AC12** — Documentation: `config.yaml` comments for every new key and
  `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` describing the model, the peak-pricing caveat and the
  per-account (non-calendar) reset dates.
- **AC13** — Post-deploy measurement: a log-derived report (reuse
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis`) shows, per account, the monthly percentage
  at the moment of reset for the first full period after deployment, and the
  target is ≥ 90% (the residual ≤ 10% being the safety margin needed for the
  rolling/weekly caps).

## Proposed approach (for the implementer to refine)

1. New module `proxy/quota_state.py`: async poller (httpx, shared client with the
   existing `server.remote_http_client` settings), per-account cache, injectable
   transport for tests (mirroring `_usage_limit_probe_transport`).
2. Wire the poller into startup/lifecycle and expose state through the existing
   metrics/status surfaces.
3. `proxy/provider.py`: extend eligibility (`_provider_in_available_window`,
   `proxy/provider.py:2378`) with a surge override, and extend chain ordering so
   `opencode-*` entries sort by effective headroom. Keep the change behind a
   single, well-named predicate so AC8's "unchanged when disabled" is easy to
   prove.
4. Config keys under `server` (defaults in brackets):
   `quota_surge_enabled` [`true`], `quota_surge_dry_run` [`false`],
   `quota_poll_interval_seconds` [`900`], `quota_surge_days` [`7`],
   `quota_exhaustion_percent` [`99.5`], `quota_state_max_age_seconds` [`3600`],
   `quota_pacing_target` [`0.95`] and an optional `quota_surge_accounts` filter
   (default: all `opencode-*` entries).
5. Optional (only if it falls out cheaply): reuse the derived
   `seconds_to_reset` to replace the *guessed* reset time in
   `_usage_limit_reset_info` for `GoUsageLimitError`, which would retire the
   guessing path from LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8 for these accounts.

## Non-goals / out of scope

- No change to the MunitoAI / DeepSeek-direct / GitHub chains (the same idea may
  later apply to `munitoai`, which does expose `x-ratelimit-*` headers —
  LP-0MVDNP36J006430L / LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ).
- No console/credit-balance API integration (none exists, finding 9).
- No per-model quota tracking (not observable, finding 3).
- Not a replacement for the existing reactive 429/`GoUsageLimitError` handling —
  it complements it.

## Risks and guards

- **Overspend risk** if a "Use balance" pay-as-you-go fallback is enabled on the
  console side → mitigated by R7/AC10 (hard stop below 100%) and by making the
  stop threshold conservative by default.
- **Peak-hour burn** → R6/AC7(e) prefer off-peak; document that surge can spend
  allowance ~2x faster per token during peak hours.
- **Blast radius on routing** → kill switch + dry-run (AC8) and the surge
  predicate scoped to `available_times` only (AC6).
- **Third-party API stability** → `/v1/usage` is undocumented on the Go page, so
  the poller must degrade gracefully (AC1) and the feature must remain safe if
  the endpoint disappears.
- **Stale state** → AC9 fail-safe revert.
- Money-relevant changes should be reviewed by the operator before merge.

## Assumptions (documented per project convention)

1. `opencode-go`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go-3` (and any future `opencode-*`
   entry) are all in scope; surge applies per entry, keyed by `api_key_env`.
2. "Monthly allowance available" means `100 - monthly.percent`, additionally
   bounded by the rolling and weekly windows (finding 2 / R2).
3. The intent is to consume the *included* allowance, not to buy pay-as-you-go
   capacity — hence the hard stop at 99.5%.
4. Importing the surge mechanism must not change behaviour for non-`opencode-*`
   providers.
5. Exact `status` values beyond `"ok"` are unknown; the implementation must treat
   anything other than `ok` conservatively (blocking) rather than optimistically.

## Related work items

- LP-0MS4ETBNO0022QAC — timed access (`available_times`), whose restriction this
  item selectively relaxes.
- LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P / LP-0MSCDOIT4008TBFQ — off-peak windows for
  opencode-hosted DeepSeek (the windows this item overrides during surge).
- LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ — `GoUsageLimitError` quarantine with computed reset.
- LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8 — guessed usage-limit quarantine locking accounts for up to
  30 days (the failure mode proactive quota reading avoids).
- LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I / LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX — blocked/open items about routing to
  `opencode-go` during off-peak windows (ordering interaction to check when
  implementing).
- LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL — per-provider request budget (`proxy/provider_budget.py`),
  the gate surge must not bypass.

## Open questions (resolved during planning)

1. Spend profile → **RESOLVED (option 1a):** keep defaults — 95% pacing target,
   99.5% hard stop, AC13 target ≥ 90% at reset. Before merge the operator should
   still confirm the console "Use balance" option is OFF on all three accounts
   (Q2 below), per the money-relevant-change review rule.
2. Is the console "Use balance" option enabled on any of the three accounts?
   **STILL OPEN — operational check for the producer** (hard stop and threshold
   defaults would be tightened if enabled on any account).
3. Surge ordering tie-break → **RESOLVED (option 2c):** score =
   `effective_headroom / seconds_to_reset`; equal/missing inputs fall back to
   config order (R3 amended; AC3's determinism wording retained).
4. Do org-scoped keys (`X-Opencode-Org-Id` appears in the endpoint's CORS
   allow-list) change the meaning of `/v1/usage` percentages? **STILL OPEN**, no
   impact on planning (not used by any plan feature).


## Plan (decomposed 2026-10-19)

Ten child features, each a vertical slice ending in tests, created in
dependency order. Test-first: the poller slice lands the shared fake-`/v1/usage`
test harness every later feature is built through; the integration/regression
slice is deliberately last.

| # | Child work item | Covers | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Quota poller and derived state (tracer bullet) (LP-0MVF7KEG7007C8MF) | AC1, AC2 (derivation), R1/R2 | — |
| F2 | Pacing model: urgency score and cap achievability (LP-0MVF7KHI5000J7BL) | AC7, R5/R6 | F1 |
| F3 | Headroom-aware opencode chain ordering (LP-0MVF7KIKE002DZVD) | AC3, R3 | F1, F2 |
| F4 | Final-week available_times surge bypass (LP-0MVF7KJN2000ASE8) | AC5, AC6, R4 | F1, F2 |
| F5 | Quota hard stop and cost guard (LP-0MVF7KO8C005NB59) | AC4, AC10, R7 | F1, F3 |
| F6 | Stale-state fail-safe, kill switch and dry-run (LP-0MVF7KPB9009U7CG) | AC8, AC9, R9 | F1, F4, F5 |
| F7 | Quota observability surface (LP-0MVF7KQED005TG9Z) | AC2 (exposure), R8 | F1, F4 |
| F8 | Configuration keys and quota-surge design doc (LP-0MVF7KRH30000KOA) | AC12, R10 | F2–F6 |
| F9 | End-to-end integration test and regression gate (LP-0MVF7KSJW007L2QF) | AC11 | F3–F7 |
| F10 | Post-deploy allowance-utilisation measurement (LP-0MVF7KTMI005B667) | AC13 | F9 |

Out of scope but tracked: Retire guessed usage-limit reset for opencode
accounts (LP-0MVF7MPZN009GOJB) — producer decision Q3 → 3a, follow-on task
blocked on this epic shipping.

Vertical slices are enforced per feature (code + tests + config key + log lines
in each). Between phases, review the next item's description and update it
(pacing/score parameters, observed log volume) before implementing.

### Plan: changelog
- 2026-10-19: decomposed into 10 features + 1 follow-on item; R3 amended to
  urgency scoring per producer decision 2c; open questions 1 and 3 resolved.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Spend target profile — (a) keep defaults 95% target / 99.5% hard stop /
  AC13 ≥90%; (b) tighter 90%/99.0%; (c) aggressive 99%/99.9%?" Answer
  (producer): "1. A". Final: keep defaults. Evidence: session
  herdr-1792407026-3930919-14977 reply "1. A 2. C 3. A".
- Q: "Ordering tie-break — (a) headroom then config order; (b) headroom then
  nearest reset; (c) score = headroom / seconds_to_reset?" Answer (producer):
  "2. C". Final: score = `effective_headroom / seconds_to_reset`; equal scores
  fall back to config order (stable). R3 amended accordingly.
- Q: "Include reusing `/v1/usage` seconds_to_reset to retire the guessed
  `_usage_limit_reset_info` path (parent proposal item 5)?" Answer (producer):
  "3. A". Final: out of scope for the epic; tracked as follow-on
  LP-0MVF7MPZN009GOJB.
- Q (operational, still open): is the console "Use balance" option enabled on
  any of the three accounts? Directed to the producer; matters because it would
  tighten the hard stop / threshold defaults before merge.
data.title: Quota-aware OpenCode Go surge: spend the full monthly allowance before it resets
